intro: Outlook for compliance analysts on Mac requires a focused approach to handle dense email chains and audit evidence. You can manage your inbox and documentation faster by using keyboard shortcuts and voice assistance to navigate the interface.
tldr: Use keyboard shortcuts to switch between Mail, Calendar, and Contacts.
Organize your audit evidence using specific folders and rules.
Leverage voice assistance to find settings or draft responses.

blocks.text: Your inbox is a primary source of audit evidence. You must keep it organized to retrieve files for regulators. Create a folder structure based on project codes or fiscal quarters. Use Outlook > Settings > Rules to automatically move incoming emails from specific stakeholders into these folders.

When you need to find an old email, use the search bar at the top right. Click the filter icon to narrow results by sender, date, or attachment type. This saves you from scrolling through thousands of messages.

If a shortcut does not work, check System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts > App Shortcuts. You can manually add the exact menu name to trigger the action. This is helpful for repetitive tasks like moving items to a specific folder.
Setting up your workspace on Mac

Microsoft now pushes the New Outlook for Mac interface. You can toggle this via the Outlook menu in the menu bar. Ensure you are running macOS 14 or later to keep receiving security updates. This is vital for maintaining the integrity of your audit logs.

If you find the Focused Inbox distracting, you can turn it off. Go to View > Focused Inbox and uncheck it. This ensures you see every email in chronological order, which is often better for monitoring audit trails.

blocks.text: Using Lazur to manage your email

You can use Lazur to navigate your inbox without clicking through menus. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where a setting is located. Lazur will draw a circle around the button on your screen. This is useful when you need to change your signature or add an account quickly.

Analysts often forget to pin important emails. Use the pin feature to keep critical requests at the top of your inbox until they are resolved. Another mistake is relying on the default search. Always use advanced filters to ensure you do not miss evidence hidden in sub-folders.

Rules are your best friend. You can move emails with specific keywords like 'Audit' or 'Compliance' into a dedicated folder. This keeps your main view clean. Go to Outlook > Rules > Edit Rules to set this up. You can also set a reminder for an email if you need to follow up on an evidence request later.

Consistency is key. If you manage multiple mailboxes, add them as shared mailboxes. This allows you to monitor all audit-related communication in one place. You can find instructions on how to add a shared mailbox in the Outlook menu.

Compliance often involves large documents. Instead of attaching files directly, upload them to your company cloud storage and share the link. This keeps your mailbox size manageable and makes version control easier. If you must send an attachment, ensure it is encrypted according to your firm policy.

faq.question: How do I switch back to legacy Outlook?
faq.answer: Go to the Outlook menu in the top bar and select 'Legacy Outlook'. Note that Microsoft is retiring support for legacy Exchange connections.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur to write emails?
faq.answer: Yes, hold the fn key to dictate your email text. Lazur will type it out at your cursor, allowing you to draft responses quickly.

faq.question: Where are my settings in the new Outlook?
faq.answer: The settings pane has moved. Click the gear icon in the bottom left or go to Outlook > Settings in the menu bar.

faq.question: Why is my email not syncing?
faq.answer: Check your network connection first. If the issue persists, go to Tools > Sync Status to see if there are any specific error codes like -3253.
